title: Stockroom Quorum Read
story: A hardware shop keeps each item's stock count on 3 replicas. Every write carries a version number one higher than the last, and counts as done once 2 replicas store it (W = 2). A read asks all 3 and waits for the first 2 answers (R = 2). Since 2 + 2 > 3, those answers always include a replica holding the latest completed write. A slow or down replica never answers.
This is the quorum read of leaderless key-value stores (see Replication and Design a Key-Value Store). It only works if the read picks the newest answer, not the first.
task: Write quorumRead(replies, r). replies lists what each replica sent, in arrival order. Each entry is [version, value], or null for a replica that timed out.

The coordinator takes the first r entries that are not null and ignores everything after them, even a newer version, because it has already answered. Return [version, value] for the highest version among those r replies. If fewer than r replicas answered, the read fails: return an empty list.
Two replies with the same version always carry the same value.

examples.explanation: The first reply is version 4 (12 in stock). The second replica timed out, so the coordinator keeps waiting. The third reply is version 5 (9 in stock). That makes 2 replies, and version 5 is newer, so the answer is 9. Returning the first reply, 12, would show stock that was already sold.

The first two replies, versions 7 and 6, already make a quorum of 2, so the coordinator answers with version 7. Version 8 arrives too late to be seen. That is allowed: R + W > N only promises that the read sees the latest write that had finished, and a write still on its way to its second replica has not finished.
Only one replica answered, and the read needs 2. Returning version 3 anyway would drop the overlap guarantee, so the read fails and the caller can retry.

hints: Which replies does the coordinator look at? What happens to one that arrives after it has r answers?
Walk the replies in order, skip the nulls, and stop once you have counted r real replies.
While walking, remember the reply with the highest version so far. Do not sort: arrival order is part of the input.
If the walk ends with fewer than r replies, return []. Otherwise return the remembered [version, value].
bruteForce: Returning the highest version in the whole list is wrong, not slow: the coordinator answers once it has r replies, so later ones never reach it (the second example).
Returning the first non-null reply is a read with R = 1, and with W = 2 on 3 replicas it can miss the latest write (the first example).

walkthrough: Simulate the coordinator: in arrival order, skip timeouts, keep the newest, and answer when the count reaches r.
• [5, 9]: 5 > 4, so best is version 5. Counted 2 = r: return [5, 9].

The limits: R + W > N guarantees the latest completed write, if both quorums come from the same N replicas. It does not order concurrent writes, and a read overlapping an unfinished write may see it while a later read does not. Read repair narrows that gap: the coordinator sends the newest value back to stale replicas it heard from.
solution.timeWhy: One pass over at most n replies, stopping early at the quorum.
solution.spaceWhy: Only the best reply and a counter.
solution.takeaway: With N replicas, W write acknowledgements and R read replies, R + W > N makes every read overlap every completed write, but only if the read returns the highest version it saw, and only once it has heard from R replicas.
